name: utmp_parse
description: Parse the binary login records wtmp, btmp, utmp and lastlog, in the layouts it names: glibc `struct utmp` (384-byte records) and `struct lastlog` (292 or 296 bytes, indexed by UID). Each record has its type, user, line, source host and address (raw bytes beside it), PID, session and time, and where it sits in the file: record index and byte offset, or UID slot. The answer names the layout and byte order it used and how it chose: a utmp byte order from the records' structure (every non-empty ut_type is 0-9 in one order only; `undetermined` where every record is empty, refused as ambiguous where both orders fit), a lastlog layout from the file size where only one width divides it or, where both do, from whether every non-empty slot's line and host are NUL-padded strings (refused as ambiguous where nothing tells them apart: pass layout; byte_order for lastlog is the little-endian default, said to be untested). Raw seconds and microseconds are kept, a tv_usec outside 0..999999 gives no time and says so, and nothing is reduced to look plausible; a short tail is named with its offset and size. A sparse lastlog is read skipping holes within max_slots and max_seconds, with next_uid to resume and uids to read only named slots. It does not read wtmpdb or lastlog2 (SQLite: refused, pointing at sqlite_query), another C library's record sizes or a 64-bit utmp time field, or a record nobody wrote: a missing record is not a login that did not happen, and a USER_PROCESS without a later DEAD_PROCESS is not shown to be open.

path.description: A wtmp, btmp, utmp or lastlog file (a link is refused; a SQLite file is refused with a pointer)

types.description: Keep only these record types, e.g. ["USER_PROCESS","BOOT_TIME"]; counts by type and boots are always over every record

user.description: Case-insensitive regex over the user name (a lastlog slot: the name from passwd, or the UID)

format.description: Force utmp or lastlog; otherwise lastlog is chosen by the file name 'lastlog'

layout.description: auto (default), utmp-384, lastlog-292 or lastlog-296. Name it where the answer says the lastlog layout is ambiguous

byte_order.description: auto (default: a utmp file's order is decided from its records), little or big

passwd.description: Optional passwd file of the evidence, used to map lastlog UID slots to account names

uids.description: lastlog only: read just the slots of these UIDs (a sparse file is not walked); the answer says its scope is the selected UIDs

start_uid.description: lastlog only: the first UID of the walk (default 0); next_uid in an earlier answer resumes it

max_slots.description: lastlog only: how many UID slots to cover in this call (holes count); the answer's next_uid says where the rest begins

max_seconds.description: lastlog only: the time to spend walking slots (default 40); what is left is named, not dropped

limit.description: Records shown inline (default 200); all are counted and, when there are more, the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.records.all_results
